learning_outcomes.text: Spatial vision skills and knowledge of graphic representation techniques, both through traditional methods of metric geometry and descriptive geometry, and through computer-aided design applications.
Knowledge and skills to apply graphic engineering techniques.

syllabus_topics: Dimensioning. General rules. Types of dimensions. Dimensioning systems
Representation of parts and assemblies. Scales
Representation of parts. Sections and Cuts
Standard representation of basic industrial elements
Representation of detachable and fixed joints
Calculation and representation of dimensional tolerances
Calculation and representation of geometric tolerances
teaching_methods: Required assignments on dihedral and axonometric representation
assessment_rules: Final grades are numerical (0-4.9 Fail, 5.0-6.9 Pass, 7.0-8.9 Good, 9.0-10 Very Good). For the ordinary call, assessment consists of practical activities (10%), partial exam (20%), final exam (60%), and application exercises (10%); for resits, the partial exam is replaced by the final exam (80%). A minimum mark of 5.0 in the final exam, and an average of 5.0 must be achieved in practical activities (with a minimum of 4.0 per activity) and application exercises (with a minimum of 4.0 per activity) to pass the module. Practical activity marks (>=5.0) are retained for the current and next academic year, while application exercise marks are only retained for the current year, and unjustified absence from over 25% of classes may bar students from the ordinary exam.
